case_name: Chanderkala Trivedi (Smt) vs Dr. S.P. Trivedi
facts_of_case: Wife's appeal against grant of decree by divorce by the High Court on ground of cruelty under Section 13(1)(ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act. The parties were married for 9 years, and the husband filed a petition for divorce due to alleged intimacy with another lady doctor.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage cannot be continued if allegations of adultery are made by the parties.
legal_principles.held: Once such allegations are made by the husband and wife as have been made in this case then it is obvious that the marriage of the two cannot in any circumstances be continued any further.
cited_cases: Narayan Ganesh Dastane v. Sucheta Narayan Dastane

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party making allegations of adultery to prove them beyond reasonable doubt.
legal_principles.held: But we do not propose to examine it as we are satisfied that the marriage is dead and the findings of fact cannot be set aside by this Court except that the appeal can be sent back to Division Bench to decide it again which would mean another exercise in futility leading to tortuous litigation and continued agony of the parties.
cited_cases: Narayan Ganesh Dastane v. Sucheta Narayan Dastane

outcome.final_order: The marriage was considered dead, and the parties were advised to arrive at a mutually acceptable resolution.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for divorce on grounds of cruelty
